notes.subject: car
notes.text: All coverage is Generation 3 trekker camera, with the same blur even where an unusual vehicle is used.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Several boat-mounted trekkers appear across the country, along coasts, rivers and atolls.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Most coverage has one or more people walking beside the trekker, a clue for both country and region.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: One official language is written in Latin letters with many long, multi-syllable words; the other is European. English shows on some commercial signs.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Climate runs from extremely dry in the south and centre to tropical in the north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Extremely broad-trunked baobab trees line the road on the famous avenue.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The southwestern national park has the reddest soil in the country's coverage.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Many palms and a blanket of white sand mark the western coastal village of Belo sur Mer.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A huge monolithic mountain with steep sides and mountainous surroundings, followed by four people.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Many palms on a brown sandy dirt road, usually with a walker in a grey T-shirt carrying a brown backpack.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Coverage along a northwestern river often shows a person in a dark blue T-shirt with sunglasses on the forehead; river boats carry two people.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Small atolls on the central west coast; the northernmost is pure sand and shore to shore is always visible, others have broad-leaved palms.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Capital coverage sits on a hillside overlooking the city, rising to the old queen's palace near the top.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The RN8 stretch between Andriamena and Marofandilia is very dry and sandy, with a large silver roof rack on the car.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The big southwestern port town looks busy and is the only large town with nobody following the trekker.
